summary: Reconcile uncertain NFS and SMB3 publication without retaining definite pre-rename failures. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The supported NFS operator workflow is unchanged; SMB3 remains gated.

api.reason: Uncertain filesystem publication uses existing needs_attention, exact readback and terminal results; routes, schema and permissions do not change.

roadmap.reason: Corrects a current destination publication and recovery gate.

state.reason: No new durable state; existing Core run, journal, catalog and repository point remain authoritative. A fresh Controller adopts the run and catalog through authenticated Core inventory.

verification.method: A focused regression failed before the fix for post-rename lost reply and passed after. The same fixture forces an actual pre-rename missing artifact and checks terminal failure with no point. Focused agent and vmhost tests plus serial full Go, Python and web checks passed; independent read-only correction review found no concrete issue. Matched disposable NFS and SMB3 members with private overlays returned lost replies after real rename and successful parent sync; each settled one run/catalog point and exact Controller replay while protected controls and old catalog/source hashes held. SMB3 retained 29 prior catalog ID/hash pairs.
verification.limits: The native NFS and SMB3 overlays simulate lost replies after successful sync; actual server sync failures remain unproven. No forge CI run exists for this candidate.
